column2: The true path runs along a rope that is not stretched high up, but just above the ground. It seems designed more to make one stumble than to be walked on.
All human errors are impatience, a premature breaking-off of method, a seeming pegging-down of a seeming thing.
From a certain point on there is no turning back. That point must be reached.
A first sign of beginning understanding is the wish to die. This life seems unbearable, another unattainable.

If you walked across a plain, had the good will to walk and yet made no progress, it would be a hopeless matter; but since you are climbing a steep slope, as steep as you yourself appear when seen from below, the setbacks may be caused only by the nature of the ground, and you must not despair.
Like a path in autumn: hardly is it swept clean when it is again covered with dry leaves.
A cage went in search of a bird.
If it had been possible to build the Tower of Babel without climbing it, it would have been permitted.
Do not let the evil make you believe you could keep secrets from it.
As firmly as the hand holds the stone. It holds it firmly only to throw it all the farther. But the way leads into that distance too.
You are the task. No pupil far and wide.
From the true adversary boundless courage flows into you.
To understand the happiness that the ground on which you stand cannot be larger than what your two feet cover.
How can one rejoice in the world, unless one flees to it?
To do the negative is still required of us; the positive is already given.
The good is, in a certain sense, comfortless.
The crows maintain that a single crow could destroy the heavens. That is beyond doubt, but proves nothing against the heavens, for heaven means precisely: the impossibility of crows.
There is no having, only being, only a being that craves its last breath, its suffocation.
Earlier I did not understand why I received no answer to my question; today I do not understand how I could believe I was able to ask. But I did not believe at all, I only asked.
One marveled at how easily he walked the road of eternity; he was, in fact, racing down it.
Only our concept of time lets us call the Last Judgment by that name; in truth it is a summary court-martial.
The disproportion of the world seems, consolingly, to be only a matter of numbers.
To believe in progress does not mean to believe that progress has already happened. That would be no belief.

A person cannot live without a lasting trust in something indestructible within himself, though both the indestructible and the trust may remain permanently hidden from him. One of the ways this hiddenness can express itself is the belief in a personal God.
One must not deceive anyone, not even the world of its victory.
There are questions we could not get past if we were not freed from them by nature.
One lies as little as possible only by lying as little as possible, not by having as little occasion to lie as possible.

Whoever renounces the world must love all human beings, for he also renounces their world. He therefore begins to sense the true human nature, which cannot be other than loved, provided one is its equal.
The fact that there is nothing but a spiritual world takes away our hope and gives us certainty.
Our art is a being dazzled by the truth: the light on the grotesque, recoiling face is true, nothing else.
He runs after the facts like a beginner at ice-skating who, moreover, is practising somewhere it is forbidden.
Theoretically there is a perfect possibility of happiness: to believe in the indestructible within oneself and not to strive toward it.
If what is said to have been destroyed in Paradise was destructible, it was not decisive; but if it was indestructible, then we live in a false belief.
Test yourself against humanity. It makes the doubter doubt, the believer believe.
The mind becomes free only when it ceases to be a support.
Truth is indivisible and therefore cannot know itself; whoever wishes to know it must be a lie.
Why do we lament over the Fall? It was not because of it that we were driven out of Paradise, but because of the Tree of Life, lest we eat of it.

We are sinful not only because we have eaten from the Tree of Knowledge, but also because we have not yet eaten from the Tree of Life. The state in which we find ourselves is sinful, independent of guilt.
Death is before us, rather like a picture of the Battle of Alexander on the wall of a classroom. What matters is to darken or even extinguish the picture through our deeds still in this life.
There can be knowledge of the diabolical, but no belief in it, for there is no more of the diabolical than there is.
Sin always comes openly and can be grasped at once with the senses. It walks on its roots and need not be torn out.
You can hold yourself back from the sufferings of the world, that is permitted to you and accords with your nature, but perhaps this very holding back is the one suffering you could have avoided.
